A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FALSE-VFL research. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original classification experiments on four datasets, including accuracy and standard deviation over five independent runs.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, and Figures 4–5 add original evaluations varying party count and missingness heterogeneity.

M1.justification: The Gaussian latent aggregation, importance-weighted objectives, two-stage training, prediction procedure, and MNAR extension remain unchanged. The added pseudocode and communication descriptions document the existing method rather than establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: The four datasets and classification tasks remain unchanged. Figure 5 adds training and testing under heterogeneous per-party missing probabilities on Isolet, HAPT, and FashionMNIST, extending the missingness environments covered.

E2.justification: Vanilla VFL, LASER-VFL, PlugVFL, and FedHSSL remain the evaluated baselines, including in the new robustness figures. Their adaptations described in Appendix D.1 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 adds two controlled evaluation designs: varying K from 4 to 12 under matched MCAR 2 and MNAR 7 training/testing, and varying Dirichlet concentration while holding average missingness at 0.2 across eight parties. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the original benchmark settings and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 4–5 add systematic robustness analyses addressing sensitivity to party count and unequal missing rates across parties on three datasets. These examine two additional robustness questions beyond the retained MCAR 5 versus MCAR 2 comparison.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five independent runs. The new analyses retain that practice; replacing shaded bands with error bars in the consolidated benchmark figure changes presentation, not statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 4–5 add substantial results on party-count and heterogeneity sensitivity, including leading FALSE-VFL accuracy and differing baseline trends; Table 3 adds sampled missing-rate entropies. The original accuracy, standard-deviation, and robustness-ratio entries are identical after matching v1 Tables 12–18 to v2 Tables 13–19.

T1.justification: Theorem C.1 changes its convergence assumption from bounded importance ratios to bounded log importance ratios and updates the proof accordingly. Section 3.1 also removes the explicit exclusion of completely missing samples. The new main-text Theorem 3.1 summarizes the existing appendix result.

C1.justification: The novelty claims and abstract's 160-of-168 comparisons with a 9.6-point average advantage remain unchanged. The conclusion explicitly extends the robustness claim to party count and data heterogeneity beyond v1's missing-rate emphasis.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 adds explanations connecting the new trends to aligned-sample availability, stability of observed representations, and LASER-VFL's utilization of batches sharing a mask. Appendix F retains the same limitation concerning inter-party MNAR dependencies.

D1.justification: Section 3.5 and Appendix A.2 newly explain communication exchanges, Appendix D.3 supplies FALSE-VFL-I pseudocode, and architecture tables specify tabular MLP depths. These refine documentation of existing components; hardware, runtimes, and listed hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 42 cited works and substantive positioning relative to VFL and missing-data methods are retained. Author-year citations and expanded bibliographic names are formatting changes.

P1.justification: The method subsections are reorganized, Section 4's numbered subsections become paragraph headings, and explanations and the conclusion are locally revised. Acknowledgments and an LLM-usage appendix are added, while Broader Impact is removed. Much of the original prose remains intact.

P2.justification: The six benchmark line-plot figures become one 24-panel bar-chart grid in v2 Figure 3. The original architecture figure is split, new robustness figures and an entropy table are added, and appendix tables are compacted. MAR captions are corrected from MAR 0/1 to MAR 1/2 without changing their numerical entries.

improvement.justification: The additional robustness studies strengthen support for practical multi-party use, while communication details, pseudocode, and the revised convergence assumption improve clarity and rigor. These are useful extensions to an already substantial evaluation. Denser figures reduce readability, and removing the explicit nonempty-observation assumption leaves that boundary less clear, but the net improvement remains supported.
